## Stage 11 — Reports / דוחות

Replaces the `/reports` placeholder with a real **Manager-only** aggregated reports page, aligned with the existing Stage 1–10 frontend foundation.

### What was implemented
- New [ReportsPage](frontend/src/pages/ReportsPage.tsx) at the existing `/reports` route (title **"דוחות"** + Hebrew manager description).
- New [ReportsDateRangeFilter](frontend/src/components/ReportsDateRangeFilter.tsx) — date range control with Hebrew validation.
- Three report sections, reusing existing components:
  - **Ticket status summary** (`TicketStatusSummary`) — all-time pending / in-progress / completed + avg completion time, from `GET /api/admin/tickets/summary`.
  - **Tickets by day** (`TicketsByDaySummary`) — created/completed/avg per day from `GET /api/admin/tickets/by-day`, with a start/end date range filter.
  - **Employee performance** (`PerformanceReportCards`) — discovers assignable Mechanic/Manager employees via `GET /api/admin/employees`, then fans out one `GET /api/admin/reports/performance?mechanic_id=` call per employee.

### Role behavior
- Manager-only (route guard unchanged: `allowedRoles('/reports')` → `['Manager']`).
- Secretary → redirected to `/dashboard`; Mechanic → redirected to `/kanban`. Neither touches the admin endpoints.

### Date range behavior
- Defaults to backend last-30-days on mount (no params).
- Applying a range re-fetches **only** the tickets-by-day section.
- `start_date > end_date` (or a missing date) shows a Hebrew validation message and does **not** call the API.

### Resilience
- Loading, empty, and error states in Hebrew, RTL, orange/amber styling.
- Core summary failure → full-page retryable error.
- Tickets-by-day and performance degrade independently to per-section "unavailable" states; one failed performance call never crashes the page.

### Intentionally NOT included
- No `EmployeeMonitoringTable` / "ניטור עובדים" — it stays in the Manager Dashboard (`/dashboard`).
- No CRUD, no charts, no backend changes, no changes to Work Board / Archive / User Management / dashboards.

- `frontend/src/components/ReportsDateRangeFilter.tsx` (new)
- `frontend/src/tests/reportsPage.test.tsx` (new)

### Verification
- `npm test` → 338 passed (33 files)
- `npm run build` → passes (tsc + vite)
- `npm run lint` → clean

### Known limitations
- Summary and performance are all-time only; only tickets-by-day supports a date range.
- Performance requires one API call per employee (no bulk endpoint).
- No quality score / ticket difficulty / real online presence — not modeled by the backend.

author: mecca-research
body:
The final "full variadics" piece: **calling external variadic stdio functions** (printf/scanf family).

```c
int ev_fwd(char *buf, int sz, const char *fmt, ...) {
  va_list ap; va_start(ap, fmt);
  int n = vsnprintf(buf, sz, fmt, ap);   // external variadic, forwarded cursor
  va_end(ap);
  return n;
}
```

## What changed

Calling `snprintf` / `vsnprintf` / `sprintf` / `printf` / `fprintf` / `sscanf` / … now lowers **like a `<math.h>` (libm) call**: an opaque external edge emitted verbatim, kept out of the R18 call graph, returning `int`. Before, an undefined callee lowered to `bcir_snprintf(...)` (a missing twin → link error) and tripped R18 ("call to undefined function"). The read-only `char[]` format string was *already* passed through as an argument — the only missing piece was recognizing the family.

- **twin** (`bcir_cfront.c`): an `is_extern_variadic` whitelist; in `p_call`, a callee **not** defined in the unit that matches the family → a `c.call.extern:<name>` claim (int result, not added to `fn->calls`), emitted verbatim.
- **oracle** (`lower`/`emit`): the same family (`_EXTERN_VARIADIC`); a callee not in `func_rets` → `c.call.extern:<name>` (int, opaque to `self.calls`), rendered verbatim.

A unit-defined function of the same name still wins (the whitelist only fires when the callee isn't in the unit).

This completes **full variadics** (#variadic + #compoundwide + this): a variadic wrapper can `va_start` its own cursor and forward it to `vsnprintf`.

## Verification

New `cfront_extvariadic.c` + `test_extern_variadic_dual_rail` (+ the `check_runtime.sh` fixture list and a dedicated behaviour section): `snprintf` with int/long/hex/width specifiers and a `vsnprintf`-forwarding variadic wrapper — the differential compares the **formatted buffer AND the returned count**.

- value differential **== Clang** on **both** the twin's and the oracle's emit (the real libc produces identical bytes)
- oracle/twin claim-count parity (`funcs=5 claims=2 … call=1 ok=1`)
- warning-clean twin (`clang -Wall -Wextra`)
- `python -m bcir.tests.run_all` green (**815 passed, 0 failed**)
- `tools/c/check_runtime.sh` green (`PASS parity cfront_extvariadic.c`, `PASS extvariadic … == Clang`)

author: the-database
body:
The worker gated rendering a future frame on sub_pts <= last_pkt_pts, treating last_pkt_pts as a decode horizon. It is not: it is the pts of the last *event* packet, and ASS event packets are sparse (one per dialogue line / sign). For a long-lived event -- exactly the dense motion-tracked sign this feature targets -- last_pkt_pts stays at the event's start, far behind the lookahead window. So every ahead frame failed the gate, was skipped (not stored), and the next loop re-found and re-skipped the same frame: a 100% busy-spin hammering both locks, which starved the playloop and made frame drops worse than baseline, even on light content.

Drop the last_pkt_pts gate entirely (the events for those frames are already in the ASS_Track once their sparse packet was demuxed, which the demuxer read-ahead does well before the worker reaches them). Keep only the pending-segment-switch guard, and when it does block, wait instead of respinning. Measured on the heavy 8K scene: worker loop iterations for 60 rendered frames went 43,343,489 -> 697; output stays pixel-identical to the synchronous path.

author: rikushimoida
body:
## 概要

プロフィール入力ページ（`/signup/profile`）でプロフィール画像を添付して「登録内容を確認」を押すと、`/signup/confirm` へ遷移せず「This page couldn't load」になるバグを修正する。

## 原因

Next.js の Server Actions はデフォルトでリクエストボディ **1MB 制限**を持つ。`apps/web/next.config.ts` に `serverActions.bodySizeLimit` の設定が無いため、デフォルトの 1MB が適用される。一方アプリ側（`saveProfileToSession`）は画像を **5MB まで**許可しており、1MB を超える画像つき FormData が Server Action 本体に到達する前にフレームワーク層で弾かれ、`Error: Body exceeded 1 MB limit.` が発生していた。

## 修正内容

- `apps/web/next.config.ts` に `serverActions.bodySizeLimit: "5mb"` を追加し、アプリ側バリデーション（5MB）とフレームワーク制限を揃えた。
  - Next.js 14.0 以降 `bodySizeLimit` は **stable** へ昇格しているため、`experimental` 配下ではなくトップレベルの `serverActions` 配下に記述（Issue 補足の `experimental.serverActions` は Next 16 では無視される）。
- 「1MB 超〜5MB 以下の画像がバリデーションを通過しアップロードされる」UT を追加。

## 受入条件

- [x] 1MB超〜5MB以下の画像を添付して送信すると Server Action に到達する（bodySizeLimit=5mb）→ UT で担保
- [x] 画像なしの送信が従来どおり成功する（回帰なし）→ 既存 UT で担保
- [x] 5MB を超える画像はアプリ側バリデーションで弾かれエラー表示 → 既存 UT で担保
- [x] preview / production / local の全環境で成立（フレームワークのデフォルト挙動のため設定で一律解消）

## テスト

- UT: `apps/web` 全 346 件パス（新規追加分含む）
- E2E: bodySizeLimit はフレームワーク設定で UT 検証不可・アプリ側バリデーションは UT で担保済みのため、テストピラミッドの原則に基づき E2E コードは追加せず。プレビュー環境での手動確認を推奨。

## 横展開所見

`bodySizeLimit` 未設定は `apps/web` 全 Server Action に影響する横断的な設定欠落。今回の修正で以下も**同時に救済される**（同一アプリ・同一設定が効くため）。受入条件外のため本PRでは E2E 確認・コード変更は伴わない。

- `apps/web/src/app/posts/new/actions.ts`（投稿作成・最大4枚画像）— 4枚合算で 1MB 超になりやすく、より確実に救済される
- `apps/web/src/app/mypage/edit/actions.ts`（プロフィール編集・base64 画像）— base64 で約1.33倍に膨らむため顕在化しやすかった

`apps/admin` の画像アップロードは API Route（Route Handler）であり Server Actions の 1MB 制限の対象外。`apps/admin/next.config.ts` への設定追加は不要。

Closes #301

author: yasirlts
body:
Brings the agent toolkit — **planning oracle**, **guardrail**, **session coherence**, and **interop CIR** — to the **Rust** and **Go** bindings, reaching full four-binding toolkit parity (the model was already four-binding; now the toolkit is too). Composes the existing Rust/Go primitives (`is_valid_transition`/`IsValidTransition`, `audit_scene`/`AuditScene`, the generated table, `money_equals`, `currency_decimals`); no invariant or transition logic is reimplemented.

## Four surfaces, each binding

- **`valid_transitions` / `ValidTransitions`** — pure read of `COMMITMENT_TRANSITIONS`; terminal → empty.
- **`guard_action`/`guard_object`** — compose transition validity + the scene audit; invalid → legal `alternatives`, over-refund → `Refunded` bounded.
- **`create_session` / `CreateSession`** — refund ledger + cumulative I-1 (probes the canonical audit with the running total).
- **`unify` + `to_stripe_action`/`to_shopify_action`/`to_woocommerce_action`** — caller-corresponded merge (mismatch → I-1, no auto-discovery); descriptor-only emitters (no network/credentials/execution).

## Behavioural equivalence is the proof

The Rust examples (`cargo run -p warp-commerce-types --example agent_guardrail|planning_oracle|agent_session|cross_platform`) and the Go example (`go run ./examples/toolkit`) run **verbatim** with the SAME verdicts as the TS/Python twins:

| scenario | verdict (all four bindings) |
|---|---|
| revert Fulfilled→Accepted | `BLOCKED [I-2]` + `[Disputed, Refunded]` |
| over-refund 500 vs 200 | `BLOCKED [I-1]`, Refunded **bounded** |
| cumulative 3×80 vs 200 | 3rd `BLOCKED [I-1]`, "240 … only 200", 40 remaining |
| unify 200 vs 150 | `BLOCKED [I-1]` not conserved |
| emit valid refund | `stripe.refund` amount **4000** (minor units), currency `mad` |

Tests mirror the suite in each binding (Rust + Go: `valid_transitions==table`, invalid→alternatives, over-refund→bounded, cumulative caught, unify rejection, emitter descriptors, no-auto-discovery, no-execution).

## Honest per-binding limits (documented, not papered over)

The Rust/Go runtimes are **conformance-focused** (deserialize + audit), so the ports document two limits — the **verdicts still match**:
1. `audit_scene`/`AuditScene` return invariant **id strings**, so `GuardViolation` messages are standard per-invariant text (message wording is binding-specific, as it already is across bindings).
2. No platform inbound mappers and no transition history-replay: `guard_action` advances a commitment's **state** to build the next world (the audit reads state vs subject for the over-refund check and validates history independently, so the verdict is unaffected), and `unify` is platform-agnostic — callers map platform objects themselves (examples build them via `serde_json` / `encoding/json`).

## Composition only; schema/conformance untouched

body:
Closes #670. Companion to #558 (gold commit, PR #669) — closes the round-trip so committed gold actually survives a reseed.

## The gap it fixes
#558 lets the GM commit a PC's live gold into `doc.gold`, but **nothing read `doc.gold` back** — gold display is driven entirely by the `cnmh_gold_<id>` overlay, which defaulted to `0` when unset. So on a fresh load / post-reseed (overlay gone) display fell back to `0`, not the committed value, and the commit was effectively write-only.

## Fix
Make the doc's gold the durable baseline and the overlay the live value on top: **default the `cnmh_gold_` overlay to `doc.gold`** everywhere it's read. `useSyncedState` (and `usePartyGold`'s seed) only fall back to the default when neither the session nor localStorage has a value, so a set overlay still wins — only an *unset* overlay now resolves to `doc.gold`.

- **`gold.js`** — `docGold(character)` helper (absent / non-finite ⇒ `0`).
- **`InventoryTab`, `PartyGoldModal`** — default the gold `useSyncedState` to `docGold(character)`.
- **`usePartyGold`** — `readLocalGold` returns `undefined` on a miss so the seed can fall back to `docGold` rather than a literal `0`.
- **`useGiveGold`** — default the giver balance to `docGold`; credit an **unset recipient** from their doc gold (so a transfer to a PC who hasn't opened their sheet doesn't wipe their gold). Reads the roster via `useContent` for the per-id lookup.

## Non-breaking
Until #558 commits gold to a doc, `character.gold` is absent and `docGold` returns `0` — byte-identical to the old literal default. So this is safe to merge before or after #669.

## Tests (58 across the touched files)
`docGold` units; `usePartyGold` doc-gold fallback + overlay-wins; `useGiveGold` unset-recipient credited from doc gold; existing InventoryTab / PartyGoldModal / GiveGoldModal suites still green. Lint clean.

author: joelsmith123
body:
Two player-facing improvements.

## 1. Hint → Random Hint + Block Hint
The single Hint button is split in two:
- **Random Hint** — unchanged behavior: places the next correct crown in the most-constrained crownless region (with auto-block + flash). `H` shortcut still triggers this.
- **Block Hint** — armed mode: click to arm, hover a colored section to highlight the whole section, click any of its tiles to reveal **that section's** crown (with the usual auto-block-on-placement). Disarms after use.

The solution stays worker-side, so Block Hint is a small promise-based `REVEAL_REGION` round-trip that resolves the chosen region's solution crown (`solutionCrownForRegion`) — isolated from the existing push-based hint channel. Reuses the existing armed-click + 900 ms flash plumbing. The two armed modes (**Block Hint** / **Block line**) are mutually exclusive.

## 2. Easier mode (toggle, default on)
Guarantees a minimum number of **one-line sections** (a colored region confined to a single row or column) by board size: **2** for n≤9, **3** for 10–12, **4** for 13–15. One-line regions pin a crown to a line, cascading naked singles — so puzzles read easier *and* verify faster.

**The number of sections is fixed at N** (one crown per color), so "more/smaller sections" is delivered as smaller, more line-shaped regions — not more of them. Average region size is fixed at N; "smaller" means lower variance (alpha 1.6→2.0) plus the guaranteed tiny line-regions.

### Construction-based — no perf compromise, no fallback
The guarantee holds **by construction**, never by generate-and-check rejection (which would inflate attempt counts):
- `planEasier` picks `threshold(n)` regions per attempt (deterministic) and pre-claims a length-2 on-line cell for each.
- `growRegions(plan)` grows those regions axis-restricted and **freezes them at the pre-claimed domino**; a pre-claim pass guarantees every region ≥2 cells; a cleanup mops up any pocket a thin strip walls off (preferring blob regions so line-regions stay one-line).
- `carveToUnique(plan)` excludes line-regions as move **TARGETS only** — a cell can still be carved *out* of one (removal keeps it on its line). This is the key refinement: protecting line cells from being moved *out* (as the original plan suggested) would block carve when an alternate merely shifts a line-region's crown within its own line, causing regrows.

**Measured** (`perf.test.ts`, attempt-count is the load-independent metric): easier p50=4 / p90≈21 vs normal p50=3 / p90≈10 — median parity, bounded tail, no rejection-sampling blow-up. The non-easier path is byte-identical (all new behavior guarded by `if (plan)`).

The setting is persisted (default on), threaded main→worker via `GENERATE`, and re-prefetches the next puzzle on toggle (token-guarded against a stale in-flight generate) so it applies to the very next New Puzzle; the current board is left untouched.

## Notes for review
- **Line-regions are size-2 dominoes** (frozen). This is the robust choice (no orphaning, flat attempt counts); it does make the *other* regions a touch larger. If you'd prefer longer/varied line-regions, that's a small follow-up (a length cap > 2) — flagging the tradeoff.
- Threshold bands resolve the spec's overlap at n=10 toward the stricter 10–12 band (`lineRegionThreshold`, trivially tunable).

## Testing
- **26 Vitest tests pass** (20 existing + 6 new): easier-mode uniqueness cross-checked vs the brute solver, an independent one-line counter ≥ threshold for n=8..15, `planEasier` distinct/on-line pre-claims, growth invariants, determinism, and a perf attempt-count guard. typecheck + build green.
- **In-browser (Preview MCP)**: easier guarantee holds live (n=9→2 one-line regions, n=15→4); Block Hint arms → highlights the section → reveals its crown + 29 auto-blocks → disarms; Block Hint/Block line mutual exclusivity; Random Hint + toggle persistence across localStorage; no console errors.

body:
## TL;DR

**What:** Continue walking configured fallback models during mid-unit rate-limit recovery and resume through the steering path after a fallback switch.
**Why:** PR #717 covered pre-dispatch model selection, but #804 reproduced the bug in the mid-unit `agent_end` recovery path: GSD displayed the fallback switch but the work still did not resume.
**How:** Reuse the shared provider-model fallback walker in transient `agent_end` recovery, and send the continuation with `deliverAs: "steer"` so the selected fallback is actually used for the resumed turn.

## What

Updates `agent-end-recovery` so rate-limit, network, server, connection, and stream recovery use the same fallback walker as provider rejection recovery. The walker skips temporarily unavailable models and keeps trying configured fallbacks before pausing.

When a fallback is selected, the recovery continuation is delivered as steering input, matching the timeout-recovery path. This covers the #804 symptom where the UI reported the fallback switch but the unit remained stopped instead of continuing on the fallback model.

Adds a behavioral regression test where the primary model hits a session limit, the first fallback is temporarily unavailable, and the second fallback is selected and immediately resumed.

## Why

Refs #716, #804. The reporter confirmed #717 did not fix the live repro because the remaining failure was not only model selection. The mid-unit recovery path also needed to use the selected fallback for the next continuation turn.

## How

The transient recovery branch now delegates fallback selection to `tryProviderModelFallback`, which already updates current unit model state, dashboard model state, skips unavailable models, and triggers a continuation turn when a fallback is selected.

The triggered continuation now uses `{ triggerTurn: true, deliverAs: "steer" }`, consistent with `auto-timeout-recovery`, so the resumed turn is steered onto the updated model state instead of waiting for the retry timer.

- Affected workflows: `/gsd auto` mid-unit provider recovery, configured model fallbacks, temporary rate-limit model blocks.
- Compatibility notes: No config format or public API changes. Existing fallback state updates and continuation behavior are reused rather than duplicated.

That path now calls **`tryProviderModelFallback`**, the same walker used for provider/model rejection, so it skips temporarily blocked or unavailable models and keeps trying configured fallbacks (then the session start model) before pausing with auto-resume.

body:
## Why

Researchers wanted a perspective to **verify the data line-by-line** — to look at the actual table instead of charts — when they want to confirm something or suspect a value is wrong. And not just the principal table: also the **derived tables that generate the charts**, so those are open to scrutiny too. **Preview-verified on real production data.**

## What

A new **"Dados (tabela)"** perspective (in *Documentação do banco*, universal). Per banco it lists the **Gold table + the serving marts that feed its charts**, and for the selected table browses the RAW rows with:
- **Server-side pagination**, **ordenação** (click a header → cycles asc/desc/off), **filtros por coluna** (`=`, `≠`, `>`, `≥`, `<`, `≤`, `contém`, `é nulo`) with removable chips, and **CSV export** of the current recorte (até 500).
- Honest loading / empty / error states; a faithful, unreshaped window (no rescaling).

### Backend — `/api/tables` + `/api/table` (security & cost by construction)
- **(banco, table) allowlist** (`gateway._INSPECT_TABLES`): only a banco's own Gold + serving marts — any other table → **HTTP 400** (no arbitrary-table reads, no Silver/Bronze).
- **The table's live schema is the column allowlist**: ORDER BY / filter columns validated against `client.get_table().schema`; filter **values stay bound `@params`**; `limit`/`offset` int-coerced. No injection surface.
- **Hybrid read**: a plain browse uses the FREE `tabledata.list` (no bytes billed); only a real sort/filter spends a query, capped by `BQ_MAX_BYTES_BILLED`. Page capped at 500 rows.

## Preview verification (real prod data)

- `/api/tables?banco=ibge_ppm` → the 2 PPM tables; **browse** `gold_ppm_production` → **2.405.516 linhas · 29 colunas**, row0 `[1980,'1980-12-31','AC','Acre'…]`.

author: jasonbhart
body:
## What changed

This PR adds a feature-flagged WhatsApp Cloud API prototype for Annalytics. It keeps Slack behavior intact while adding a gated WhatsApp path that can receive one-to-one text questions, run them through the existing analytics pipeline, and return compact plain-text responses.

Key pieces included:

- WhatsApp config/env support behind `WHATSAPP_ENABLED=false` by default.
- Cloud API webhook verification and raw-body signature handling.
- Payload parsing into normalized channel messages and unsupported-message notices.
- Minimal Cloud API text sender and WhatsApp-safe plain-text renderers.
- Firestore-backed inbound event dedupe with TTL manifest coverage.
- Allowlist, rate limit, clarification resume, pending-escalation guard, and pipeline orchestration for WhatsApp messages.
- Response context persistence with WhatsApp-safe Firestore document IDs.
- Health/doctor metadata for WhatsApp configuration state.
- Design/plan/governance docs for the prototype boundary.

## Review hardening

The latest patch addresses the review findings before publication:

- ACK messages are now non-terminal for dedupe. A WhatsApp inbound event is marked durable only after a terminal answer, clarification, safe error, rate-limit, pending-escalation, or unsupported-message reply is actually delivered.
- Unsupported non-text messages now go through the same allowlist and dedupe handler path as text messages. The webhook no longer sends unsupported replies directly.

## Why not OpenWA

OpenWA is intentionally not part of this PR. It depends on browser/session automation around WhatsApp Web, which is brittle for a production Cloud Run service, harder to operate headlessly, and sits outside Meta's official WhatsApp Business Platform path. It would also create session persistence and account-ban risk that does not fit this repo's trust-first prototype boundary.

The Cloud API route is the right fit here because it is official, webhook-based, token-driven, deployable on Cloud Run, and aligns with the existing Express/Bolt HTTP service model. It does require Meta Business/WhatsApp Cloud API setup, but it avoids introducing a browser automation runtime into the application.

author: stevemoodie
body:
Closes #501.

## Problem
A user's edited **display name** lives only in the control plane (`launchpad-users.displayName`, edited in Profile), but **Stock Analyser / Budget Tracker render the token `given_name`** (`user.name` = `composeDisplayName`). The two were disconnected — the name you set in Profile never reached SA/BT.

## Fix — approach A (pre-token projection)
The **pre-token-generation trigger projects the control-plane displayName into the token's `display_name` claim**; `composeDisplayName` prefers it. The control-plane displayName becomes the single source of truth: the name set in Profile shows in **every** app (all read `user.name` from the token), and survives re-federation (projected fresh each token, never stored on the Cognito user — it also obsoletes any directly-set `given_name` sentinel).

### Load-bearing care (this is the pre-token trigger — #486/#473 lived here)
- **#494 precedence preserved.** New order: `displayName → given+family → name-claim → given → email LOCAL part`. The chain below the new top entry is **unchanged** — nothing changes for users who haven't set a displayName (claim omitted ⟹ exact #494 behaviour). Covered by tests.
- **Native + federated.** The displayName is read keyed on the **sub** (`membershipUserId`) — the same #486 federated-keying path that the membership query uses — so a federated user's projected name comes from their own row, not the provider-shaped Username. Read failures **fail open** (no claim). Added a federated-shaped test.
- No app code changed — apps keep reading `user.name`.

## Caveat (documented, by design)
Cross-app it is **eventually consistent**: an app reflects a changed name on its **next token refresh** (Amplify caches ~1h). The launchpad updates immediately on save (#500). We deliberately do **not** force-refresh every app load just for names (perf cost).

## Changes
- `composeDisplayName` (`packages/auth-client`): new top-priority `displayName` source + tests.
- `cognito-auth`: reads the `display_name` claim → `user.name`.

## Shipped: running-heart-rate-zones

Prog Strength now computes a five-zone, percent-of-max heart-rate breakdown for every running activity and surfaces it as an additive `heart_rate_zones` block on the activity response, with a hand-rolled zones widget on the web running detail page. It answers the question a run's average HR can't — *what kind of work the run did* — and self-calibrates the athlete's reference max HR over time so no manual max-HR entry is needed.

**SOW**: [`sows/running-heart-rate-zones.md`](https://github.com/Prog-Strength/prog-strength-docs/blob/main/sows/running-heart-rate-zones.md)

## Implementation PRs

- [`prog-strength-api#57`](https://github.com/Prog-Strength/prog-strength-api/pull/57) — new pure `internal/hrzones` engine (zone model + cold-start→calibrated reference-estimation ladder), `[hr_zones]` config section, `activity.RecentHRStats` repository read, and the additive `heart_rate_zones` block on `GET /activities/{id}` (omitted for runs with no HR).
- [`prog-strength-web#100`](https://github.com/Prog-Strength/prog-strength-web/pull/100) — heart-rate zones widget on the running detail page: stacked time-in-zone bar + legend, periwinkle zone ramp tokens, and a "calibrating" banner that clears once the estimate is trustworthy.

## Deployment

1. **`prog-strength-api`** (#57) — merge and deploy first. It adds the `heart_rate_zones` field the web widget reads; until the API is live the field is simply absent. The change is additive and non-breaking (no migration), so existing clients are unaffected — but the feature isn't observable until this deploys.
2. **`prog-strength-web`** (#100) — merge and deploy after the API is live. The widget renders nothing when `heart_rate_zones` is absent, so deploying it before the API is harmless but pointless; deploy it once the API responds with the block so the widget actually appears.

No database migration and no coordination window beyond this order — the field is read-time-derived and additive.

## Verification after rollout

- Open a running activity that has heart-rate data → the zones widget renders under the stats band: a stacked time-in-zone bar plus a per-zone legend (name, bpm range, time, percentage), with the five segment widths summing across the run.
- Confirm `GET /activities/{id}` for that run returns a `heart_rate_zones` object: `model: "percent_max_hr"`, five `zones`, and `time_pct` values that sum to ~1.0.
- Open a run with **no** heart-rate data → no widget, and the response has no `heart_rate_zones` key.
- For a brand-new / lightly-logged athlete, confirm the **"Calibrating — zones will sharpen…"** banner shows and `reference_confidence` is `estimated`/`calibrating`; after enough HR-bearing runs accumulate in the recency window, confirm the banner clears and `reference_confidence` becomes `calibrated`.

---

body:
## Why
Two gaps an op-spawned agent in **any** project hit — the same class as the KB on-demand gap, the operator's exact worry:
- **(b) "work to the current objective"**: in lean spawn mode the project docs are only **INDEXED**, never bodied — so the live `current_objective` (the single highest-signal *"what we're doing right now"*) was a one-line index entry the agent had to remember to `doc_read`. It often didn't.
- **(a) "proactively use the cortex note tools"**: the footer's write guidance was soft, so agents waited to be reminded instead of maintaining `current_objective` / journaling on their own.

(The note tools + their instructions already reach every op session via the auto-attached memory MCP — this PR makes the **current objective** and the **proactive-write** behaviour reliable.)

## Fix — both in `renderLeanSpawn`
1. **Always inject the `current_objective` BODY** (when non-empty) as a dedicated **`### Current objective — work to THIS`** block, right after the binding foundational rules and before the doc index. Short by design (~hundreds of tokens) → the agent gets its working brief without a fetch.
   - FULL mode already bodies `inject=true` sections, so this closes the **lean-mode** gap specifically (lean is the live mode).
2. **Strengthen the footer** into an imperative **PROACTIVE-maintenance** directive: work to the current objective; call `current_objective_set` yourself when it changes (new / done / steps shift — direct write, no approval); `session_log_append` on every meaningful step / decision / blocker; `memory_store` durable facts. `goal`/`plan` stay propose-only.

- [ ] Post-deploy: set a real current_objective on a project, spawn a session, confirm the agent opens by working to it and updates it as work progresses.

- Frozen projects inject no objective (the block is inside the `!frozen` branch); a project with no current_objective just shows the footer's "if none is set… set one".
